subject: fennec
pitch: A fennec fox kit standing alert on a little sand dune at dusk. Enormous satin ears lined in pale peach, cream fur warming to sandy gold along its back, a fluffy tail with a smudge of black at the tip, and big dark eyes with a tiny white sparkle. Its paws are a touch oversized, like it hasn't grown into them yet, and it wears a woven leather collar with a small brass bell.
reasoning:
I'm planning the scene layout: a small fox kit standing atop a flattened dune mound, with the dune base at ground level and the kit's proportions scaled around 0.3m tall, ears bringing it closer to 0.38m.

Now I'm working out the skeleton hierarchy for the fox — establishing joint coordinates for the hips, spine chain, and neck, while also setting up the dune as a lathe shape with a rounded, mottled sandy profile built from a sequence of outline points.

Still defining body radii and sweep shapes...

Still placing facial features...

I'll simplify the eye by just increasing its radius slightly instead of adding a separate rim detail. For the ears, I'm planning a large leaf-shaped extrusion with gold-cream outer and peach inner layers, attaching them via a joint on the head and working out the orientation vectors so the shape faces forward correctly.

Working out ear geometry...

Working out leg segment lengths and bend directions, computing front leg reach from shoulder to paw and hind leg digitigrade geometry with hip, ankle, and foot joints.

Planning oversized paws with gradient-shaded legs fading from gold to cream, plus small ellipsoid foot pads and tiny toe spheres in a peachy tan for the fennec's feet.

Working out how the paws sink into the dune's surface -- aligning foot targets to the lathe-shaped dune profile, adjusting the slope so the plateau is wider and flatter with the peak raised slightly for a more natural resting position.

I'm deciding to skip adding ripple texture or scattered rocks for simplicity, leaning on surface color variation instead, and now moving on to figuring out the overall model height including the ear placement above the head.

With the head joint around y 0.31 and ears being proportionally huge like a real fennec's, I'm letting the ear tips reach up to about 0.5 in height. For the tail, I'm chaining a curve of points sloping down and back from the hips, keeping it just high enough to clear the dune surface.

Now I'm defining tail shading with a gradient that's sandy gold countershaded against cream underneath, and darkening near the black tip, plus setting up the radius profile so the tail tapers and puffs out fluffily along its length with round end caps. Next I'm sketching a collar by wrapping a surface loop around the neck sweep.

For the collar itself, I'm planning a woven leather belt texture — brown base with darker stripe banding computed from the angular position around the loop, so it reads as a braided pattern circling the neck.

Then I'm adding a brass bell hanging at the front-bottom of the collar loop, figuring out the angle convention to place it correctly.

Working out the collar loop orientation using the chain point's tangent frame, and figuring out the bell placement by casting a ray toward the underside of the neck tube to find the attachment point.

Adding the bell ring and slit using small offset geometry, then wiring up the part to the nearest neck joint so the bell hangs naturally before moving on to the chest fluff.

Now I'm planning the coat colors—gold, cream, peach, dark, black tail, leather, brass, and sand tones—and applying a countershaded paint scheme to the head sphere so it blends from cream toward a warmer sandy gold along the back.

I'm defining a helper function to position features on the head using forward, up, and left offsets, and starting to block out the snout shape, nose, and eye markings.

Now I'm sketching the mouth geometry: an upper snout frustum tapering toward the nose, a lower jaw frustum hinged at the jaw joint, and a small dark nose sphere at the snout tip, all positioned using the head-local coordinate helper.

Moving to the skull itself: a wide scaled sphere for the head, plus cheek tufts made of small spikes angled outward and down from each side, colored cream and bound to the head bone with a slight forward-downward facing direction.

Adding roundness with chest, hip, and shoulder spheres positioned and scaled onto the spine, then sweeping the spine chain with tapered radii for body volume -- checking that the body sits high enough above the dune and that leg lengths bridge the gap down to the feet properly.

For the legs I'm building sweep geometry with varying radius along the chain, then placing paw spheres at the final tip joint position with a slight offset, plus three small toe spheres spaced across the front of each paw.

I'm deciding whether to add extra dune details like ripple decals, scattered rocks, or grass tufts -- skipping most of these but considering a small cluster of grass spikes near the dune surface, though I'm wary of how bone assignment might behave for decorative elements without their own joints.

Settling on assigning the dune and grass to the hips bone for simplicity, and setting up the lathe shape for the dune with 16 segments and sandy mottled coloring, positioned at the origin. I'm also working through the joint hierarchy -- hips at the root, jaw parented to head, and head parented to the neck's second joint with a defined direction and role, before moving into defining the spine chain.

Now I'm chaining the spine and neck joints into named segments, then positioning the ears: aiming the ear joint from the head with a forward-leaning direction, defining the ear base and setting its hinge role before extruding the ear bone mirrored across both sides.

For coloring, I'm picking fennec-style ear tones -- a golden-tan outer hue with a peachy-cream inner shade to match the fur gradient.

Adding dark-rimmed eye spheres with a slightly flattened shape for a more natural look, and sketching in three thin whisker spikes per side extending from the muzzle.

Then I'm moving on to the neck collar: building a path along the neck's tangent frame at a chosen point, sweeping a small box-section profile along it to form a woven leather collar with alternating stripe colors.

I add brass stud spheres spaced along the collar loop, then find where a bell should attach by finding the nearest point on the neck surface below center and offsetting slightly along its normal to place a small brass bell sphere.

Now I'm writing the sweep code for the neck mesh and tail chain, using catmull-rom points for the tail path with color bands transitioning from the tail coat color to black at the tip.
